fullTitle: A Poultry Management System with Weight-Based Feed Dispensing and Water Level Monitoring Device
course: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
school: College of Engineering, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng San Pablo · May 2026
tagline: A poultry management system with weight-based feed dispensing and water level monitoring.
problem: A poultry farm in San Pablo City, Laguna, primarily raises laying hens for egg production and continues to perform feeding and watering activities manually. This practice requires workers to regularly inspect feed supplies, distribute feed, and check water levels.

Without weight-based feed measurement and timely notifications regarding low supply levels, maintaining consistent feeding quantities and responding promptly to resource shortages can become challenging. Manual feeding and watering can lead to worker fatigue, can be time consuming, and unmeasured feed can result in inconsistent feed and water for the chickens.

The absence of automated data collection may also limit the availability of accurate operational records for reviewing feeding activities and system conditions. Because traditional methods rely on visual observation, farmers cannot accurately quantify how much feed or water is consumed, so changes such as decreased intake can go unnoticed.
generalObjective: To help poultry farm owners in San Pablo City, Laguna, optimize their daily operations by designing and developing an automated poultry management system with weight-based feed dispensing and water-level monitoring that uses the Arduino Mega 2560 as its main controller and the ESP32 as its communication controller for Wi-Fi-based data transmission to a mobile application. The system aims to reduce manual labor, minimize feed wastage through weight-based dispensing, improve monitoring of feed and water availability, and support consistent poultry management.

specificObjectives.text: Design and develop an enhanced automated poultry management device, building upon existing feeding and watering systems, with the following functions:

items.label: a
items.text: Implementing programmable feeding schedules that can be adjusted according to the nutritional requirements of the flock.

items.label: b
items.text: Dispensing user-defined quantities of feed through integrated load cell sensors (HX711) to ensure accurate weight-based distribution and minimize feed wastage.

items.label: c
items.text: Monitoring feed level within the storage hopper to maintain sufficient supply and prevent operational interruptions.

items.label: d
items.text: Terminating feed dispensing automatically once target weights are reached and resetting the mechanism for subsequent operational cycles.

items.label: e
items.text: Implementing a data-logging feature using Google Sheets to record feeding schedules, feeding activities, dispensed feed weights, water-level status, and system operations. Authorized users can access the stored records directly through Google Sheets using the mobile application, while the Nextion display presents only selected information retrieved from Google Sheets through the system's communication and backend services.

items.label: f
items.text: Monitoring the water level in the main water container through a float switch and notifying the user when the water reaches the designated low-level threshold.

items.label: g
items.text: Providing a Nextion display interface that interactively displays the system status, including operational states, feed weight, feed level, water level, and scheduled feeding times, for effective on-site monitoring.

items.label: h
items.text: Developing a mobile application that allows users to remotely monitor system information and receive notifications regarding low feed levels and water levels that reach the designated threshold.

items.label: i
items.text: Implementing a data-logging feature using Google Sheets to record feeding schedules, feeding activities, dispensed feed weights, water-level status, and system operations. The recorded information will be accessible through the mobile application and Nextion display through the system's communication and backend services.

specificObjectives.text: Evaluate using ISO/IEC 25010 following functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, interaction capability, reliability, security, maintainability, flexibility, and safety which will ensure the overall quality of the designed project.
Deploy the device to a poultry farm in San Pablo City, Laguna.

steps.title: Go home
steps.text: The hopper rides the chain to its home position over the middle of tray 1 and stops at the limit switch.

steps.title: Weigh every tray
steps.text: The scale under each tray reports how much feed is already there.

steps.title: Pour what is missing
steps.text: Over each tray, in the order 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, the auger pours three drops that together make up only the missing grams.

steps.title: Top up
steps.text: After the last drop the tray is weighed again and a short extra pour closes any remaining gap.

steps.title: Return and report
steps.text: The hopper returns home, and the results go to the app as device data through the ESP32.

functions.title: Pours only the missing amount
functions.what: Each tray is weighed before feeding, so a tray that still has feed gets only the difference. A full tray gets nothing.

functions.title: Feeds on a schedule
functions.what: Up to three daily feeding times are saved on the machine, and a clock module keeps them on time even when the internet is down.

functions.title: Manual feed from the app
functions.what: Set the grams per tray in the mobile app and start a feed from anywhere with internet.

functions.title: Feed Now on the panel
functions.what: Start a feed from the touch screen on the machine. Dispensing stops once each tray reaches its target, and the hopper returns home ready for the next cycle.

functions.title: Low-feed alert
functions.what: The level sensor watches the hopper. When feed runs low the buzzer sounds and the app shows an alert.

functions.title: Low-water alert
functions.what: A float switch in the reservoir drops when the water runs low. The buzzer sounds and the app shows an alert.

functions.title: Monitoring in the app
functions.what: The app shows tray weights, hopper level, water status, feeding history and alerts, with timely updates.

functions.title: Touch screen control
functions.what: The 7-inch screen on the machine shows status, schedules, history and a system check.

notes: A second 50 g feed, with every tray already at its target, poured nothing.
Very small amounts are not precise. A 10 g target landed between 8 and 20 g, because the auger drops pellets in clumps.
The hopper level is an estimate. Its sensor sits above the auger, and a dip in the feed can make it read low.
